segment_text: Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) ARTICLE 14 CONFIDENTIALITY 14.1 Definition. As used in this Agreement, the term "Confidential Information" means any information disclosed by one Party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") pursuant to this Agreement which is (a) in written, graphic, machine readable or other tangible form and is marked "Confidential", "Proprietary" or in some other manner to indicate its confidential nature, or (b) oral information disclosed pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such information is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure and reduced to a written summary by the Disclosing Party, within thirty (30) calendar days after its oral disclosure, which is marked in a manner to indicate its confidential nature and delivered to the Receiving Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Disclosing Party's failure to so mark any of its Confidential Information, whether disclosed in written, graphic, machine readable or other tangible form, or its failure to designate as confidential and reduce to writing any Confidential Information disclosed orally, shall not relieve the Receiving Party of its obligations hereunder with respect to such Confidential Information if its confidential nature would be apparent to a reasonable person in the biotechnology or biopharmaceutical industry, based on the subject matter of such Confidential Information or the circumstances under which it is disclosed.

rule: section 2 (1-3 obligation-bearing clause band)
reason: Four distinct modality-bearing clauses: (1) MUST -- Rigel shall supply Kissei with the Product and placebo; (2) MUST -- Kissei shall perform Finish Manufacture for Development uses; (3) MAY -- Kissei may perform the capsule appearance test and Finish Manufacture for Commercial uses; (4) MUST -- Kissei shall be responsible for ensuring Applicable Laws/Regulatory Approvals compliance. (2) and (3) share the Finish-Manufacture phrase but differ in modality (MUST vs MAY) and object scope (Development vs Commercial) -- different modality rules out merging under section 4.3/8.3 since Obligation holds one modality. Four clauses exceeds section 2's 1-3 band.

rule: section 2 (party's right, no correlative duty) as clarified by new section 2.5
reason: Sentence 1 ('nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating any exclusive arrangement...') is an interpretive/construction clause, non-party subject, same shape as C04-163's already-excluded savings clauses. Sentence 2 ('Miltenyi reserves the right, at its sole discretion and without any restriction or limitation whatsoever, to manufacture, have manufactured, use, have used, sell, have sold, offer for sale, export, import or otherwise commercialize or dispose of Miltenyi Products in any manner and for any purpose whatsoever') is a broad, unrestricted, no-correlative-party rights-reservation -- reviewer-ruled at this item as the motivating example for new section 2.5, which clarifies section 2's own 'party's right, no correlative duty' row: the test is whether the clause has a future state worth monitoring (a correlative party, a deadline, a gating condition), not whether it is grammatically a MAY. This clause has none -- unrestricted scope, no correlative party, a ten-verb catch-all enumeration whose purpose is legal completeness, not ten distinct actions. Same underlying principle as section 3.2.1's hereby-clause exclusion, reached from the opposite surface pattern (an ongoing entitlement rather than a completed act).

reason: Entire-agreement / conflicting-provisions boilerplate, three sentences, no party subject anywhere and no 'shall'/'must'/'may' in the segment at all. rule: section 8.8.1 (negated-entitlement copular class, v0.41-added), section 3.2.1 (hereby-performative)
reason: Excluded on two independent grounds, each covering one half of the sentence. GROUND 1 (section 8.8.1, reviewer-ruled and added at v0.41, citing this item as the confirming instance): '(c) No Principal shall have any right of subrogation, repayment, reimbursement or indemnity whatsoever, unless and until the Obligations are paid or performed in full' is a copular status/entitlement statement, not commanded conduct -- the identical class section 8.8 already names for the affirmative form ('shall not be liable/entitled'), now confirmed to cover the negated-object form too ('shall have no right of X') since negation placement does not change which test the class applies (does the clause command/forbid conduct, or describe a status?). No party is being told to do or refrain from doing an act; the clause states that a Principal does not currently hold subrogation rights. GROUND 2 (section 3.2.1, direct application, no extension needed): 'and all debts owed by the Franchisee to any Principal are hereby subordinated to the Obligations' is a present-tense self-executing performative ('are hereby subordinated') -- the identical class already covers 'hereby grants'/'hereby assigns'/etc: it takes full legal effect at execution (the moment this document is signed, the described debts become subordinated by operation of the clause itself), leaving no future state to monitor. The segment is a self-contained list item (its own subject 'No Principal' and modal 'shall have', unlike the orphan-list-item exclusions C04-024/C22-025 earlier in this batch) but both of its clauses independently fail to state an obligation, so no item is drafted from it.

reason: Survival boilerplate. 'The following Articles and Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement, including the rights and obligations of each Party thereunder: Article I; Article V; this Article VI; Article VII; Article IX; and Article X.' Subject is 'The following Articles and Sections' (contract provisions, a thing), not a party; 'shall survive' states which provisions remain in legal effect after termination, a status/legal-effect statement rather than any party's duty -- the identical class already excluded today at C10-029 (severability) and E08-046 (deemed-delivery), and at C22-045/C04-045-shaped entire-agreement clauses in earlier batches. 'SURVIVE' is not a taxonomy action verb and there is no party performing an act to map one onto. No obligation-bearing sentence in the segment.
segment_text: Section 6.5 Survival. The following Articles and Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement, including the rights and obligations of each Party thereunder: Article I; Article V; this Article VI; Article VII; Article IX; and Article X.

rule: section 2 (exceeds the 1-3 obligation-bearing clause band)
reason:
A coherent, well-formed subcontracting provision -- not a table artifact like C17-077 -- that nonetheless resolves to 6 distinct obligation-bearing clauses once the content is correctly analyzed, double section 2's 1-3 band: (1) 'NICE may choose...to enable any NICE Affiliate to act on NICE' behalf...' (MAY, obligor NICE, correlative party Contractor); (2) 'Contractor may sub-contract some of its obligations ("PERMITTED SUBCONTRACTORS")...' (MAY, obligor Contractor, conditioned on NICE's prior written approval); (3) 'Contractor shall provide to NICE material qualifications and identification details of such Permitted Subcontractors' (MUST, clean PROVIDE match); (4) 'Contractor shall at all times remain fully responsible for the performance of all obligations of Contractor hereunder, jointly and severally with the Permitted Subcontractors' (MUST -- see ruling below); (5)-(6) 'Contractor shall comply with all reasonable NICE vendor screening requirements...and Contractor shall also comply with its own vendor screening requirements' splits into two independently-breachable clauses (see ruling below). Excluded mechanically on the same band ground as C17-077, no exception made despite the analysis already invested -- eligibility is decided before content is adjudicated, and the reviewer explicitly declined to let sunk analysis cost bias the eligibility call. Second batch-3 instance of a segment exceeding the band without being a single-sentence chaining case; see section 2's new observational note (v0.41) -- not resolved, flagged for a possible third instance.

TWO JUDGMENT CALLS WERE RESOLVED BEFORE THE BAND ISSUE WAS CAUGHT, AND ARE PRESERVED HERE AS FORWARD GUIDANCE (not cashed in on this segment, citable if this shape recurs on an in-band segment): (A) 'Contractor shall remain obligated under this Agreement' (a trailing qualifier on clause (2) above) and clause (4) ('...remain fully responsible...jointly and severally...') are a section 4.3.1 RESTATEMENT of the same accountability fact, not two items and not a section 8.8.1 copular-status exclusion -- REVIEWER-RULED: 'remain fully responsible...jointly and severally' actively allocates real, checkable accountability for subcontractor performance, which is genuine obligation-bearing content, not a status description with nothing to monitor; section 8.8.1's own test ('status/right description with nothing to monitor') does not reach this pattern, and extending it here would have been an unchecked third application of a rule written earlier the same session. Had this segment been in-band, clause (4) (the more complete phrasing -- 'at all times', 'jointly and severally', 'all obligations') would have been the item's span, with clause (2)'s trailing tail recorded as the redundant echo per section 4.3.1 step 2. (B) The vendor-screening sentence splits into TWO items under section 4.3's 'notify and remedy' shape, not its 'deliver...and keep current' shape -- REVIEWER-RULED: Contractor could satisfy NICE's screening requirements while violating its own, or vice versa, the independently-breachable signature that requires a split; different object (NICE's requirements vs. Contractor's own) even with the identical verb (COMPLY) and obligor (Contractor).
segment_text: It is further clarified that NICE may choose, by written notice to Contractor, to enable any NICE Affiliate to act on NICE' behalf and in its name under this Agreement directly VIS-A-VIS Contractor, without relieving NICE as the sole contractual party from responsibility for performance of the Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Upon NICE' prior written approval and upon the terms and limitations of such approval, Contractor may sub-contract some of its obligations ("PERMITTED SUBCONTRACTORS"), provided, however, that Contractor shall remain obligated under this Agreement. Contractor shall provide to NICE material qualifications and identification details of such Permitted Subcontractors. Contractor shall at all times remain fully responsible for the performance of all obligations of Contractor hereunder, jointly and severally with the Permitted Subcontractors. In selecting subcontractors to assist Contractor in the performance of this Agreement, Contractor shall comply with all reasonable NICE vendor screening requirements which are provided to it, and Contractor shall also comply with its own vendor screening requirements.

rule: section 3.8.1 / section 8.8 (copular 'shall be deemed' compliance-status class)
reason: '(xxv) so long as the GOB Sale is conducted in accordance with the Sale Guidelines and the Approval Order and in a safe and professional manner, Purchaser shall be deemed to be in compliance with any Applicable General Laws;' -- 'Purchaser shall be deemed to be in compliance with X' is a legal-fiction/safe-harbor deeming clause about compliance STATUS, not commanded conduct; Purchaser is not being told to do anything beyond what the leading 'so long as' clause already describes. Same copular-deeming class already excluded today at E08-046 ('shall be deemed to have been delivered') and matching section 3.8.1's own worked non-branch-1 example ('the Gas shall be deemed dry'). Unlike C11-101 (this batch) or E08-046, the grammatical subject here IS a party (Purchaser), but the predicate is still a status assertion, not conduct -- the same distinction section 8.8.1 draws for negated entitlement, now confirming a third surface form (a deeming/safe-harbor clause) reaches the identical non-obligation class without needing any further rule extension, since section 3.8.1 already named 'deemed' clauses as non-branch-1 directly.

rule: section 2 (exceeds the 1-3 obligation-bearing clause band)
reason:
A dense NICE-supplied-components provision that reads as at least 5-7 distinct obligation-bearing clauses even under the most conservative merge-everything reading, well beyond section 2's 1-3 band: (1) 'NICE may, at its election, supply to Contractor software licenses and software...' (MAY); (2) 'All 12 such components will be delivered to Contractor in a mutually agreed package type...' (MUST-ish, agentless passive); (3) 'The parties will agree on the inventory level required by Contractor for each NICE Component' (MUST/NEGOTIATE, collective obligor); (4) 'NICE' sole responsibility shall be to renew the inventory upon request' (MUST); (5) 'Contractor shall be responsible for ordering additional NICE Components if required above the inventory level and for ensuring that appropriate physical controls of such components are in place and properly administered' (at least 1, likely 2 -- two independently-breachable performances); (6) 'Contractor will not charge NICE any charges or overhead for such NICE Components' (MUST_NOT); (7) a second, conditioned restatement of (6) later in the segment (possibly section 4.3.1, possibly distinct -- unresolved). Excluded mechanically on the same band ground as C17-077 and C14-139, clause-count check run FIRST this time before any individual field-level judgment call was drafted -- the C14-139 process fix held.

THREE QUESTIONS PRESERVED AS FORWARD GUIDANCE, NOT RESOLVED, NAMED PRECISELY FOR CITATION IF THIS SHAPE RECURS: (A) SUSPECTED SECTION 8.7 ARTIFACT, NOT CONFIRMED -- clause (2)'s 'All 12 such components will be delivered' reads as a spliced page-number ('12') inside 'All such components', the identical mid-sentence-splice shape section 8.7 already names (previously measured concentrated in C04/C06/E07/CUAD-Source-footer/C22/E01/C05; C14 not previously checked for this class). Not verified against the raw C14.txt source in this session -- if this segment is ever revisited, check page boundaries before assuming. (B) RESTATEMENT-VS-DISTINCT, SAME SHAPE AS C14-139's Q1, NOW A SECOND INSTANCE -- clause (7) restates clause (6)'s no-charge duty with an added leading conditional clause (Contractor's purchasing difficulty + NICE's consent, which is exactly the scenario clause (1) already describes). Section 4.3.1 step 1's literal test (any scored field differs -> distinct) would call these distinct since conditions differ; but the same 'more complete restatement of an identical real-world fact' reasoning that resolved C14-139's Q1 could apply here too. Worth watching for a third instance before deciding which test wins when they conflict. (C) TWO-INDEPENDENTLY-BREACHABLE-PERFORMANCES SPLIT, SAME SHAPE AS C14-139's Q2, NOW A SECOND INSTANCE -- clause (5)'s 'ordering additional NICE Components' and 'ensuring appropriate physical controls...are in place' are plausibly two separate, independently-breachable performances (Contractor could order components correctly while failing physical-control administration, or vice versa), the identical 'notify and remedy' shape as C14-139's vendor-screening split. Not resolved here either.
segment_text: 2.5. NICE SUPPLIED COMPONENTS. NICE may, at its election, supply to Contractor software licenses and software or the like for which NICE has an existing royalty agreement with a third party (except electrical and mechanical components unless agreed otherwise), in lieu of Contractor purchasing same ("NICE COMPONENTS"). All 12 such components will be delivered to Contractor in a mutually agreed package type, and in an agreed upon time and in agreed upon quantities. The parties will agree on the inventory level required by Contractor for each NICE Component and NICE' sole responsibility shall be to renew the inventory upon request. Contractor shall be responsible for ordering additional NICE Components if required above the inventory level and for ensuring that appropriate physical controls of such components are in place and properly administered. Contractor will not charge NICE any charges or overhead for such NICE Components. In the event Contractor has difficulty in purchasing any components which NICE can obtain and NICE has granted its consent to supply such component to Contractor in lieu of Contractor purchasing same, Contractor will not charge NICE any charges or overhead for such Components.

rule: section 2 (no obligation-bearing clause -- subject is an event, savings/interpretive provision, section 3.8.1's own non-branch-1 example class)
reason: Survival-of-obligations savings boilerplate, two sentences, both non-party-subject. (1) 'Termination, relinquishment or expiration of the Agreement for any reason shall be without prejudice to any rights which shall have accrued to the benefit of either Party prior to...such termination, relinquishment or expiration.' -- subject is 'Termination, relinquishment or expiration' (an event), an interpretive/savings statement about how already-accrued rights are treated, not a party's duty. (2) 'Such termination, relinquishment or expiration shall not relieve either Party from obligations that are expressly indicated to survive termination or expiration of the Agreement.' -- same subject, same class. Both sentences are the identical shape section 3.8.1 already names as its own worked non-branch-1 example ('an interpretive or savings provision with a non-party subject'), and near-identical in structure to C04-163's already-excluded savings clause ('The termination of this Agreement...shall not operate to relieve Bellicum from its obligation to pay...'). No party subject anywhere in the segment; no obligation-bearing sentence.
segment_text: (g) Termination, relinquishment or expiration of the Agreement for any reason shall be without prejudice to any rights which shall have accrued to the benefit of either Party prior to (or as a result of, including, without limitation, rights available under law and equity) such termination, relinquishment or expiration. Such termination, relinquishment or expiration shall not relieve either Party from obligations that are expressly indicated to survive termination or expiration of the Agreement.

rule: section 2.5.1
reason: 'NICE may, at its discretion, reschedule delivery of units of Products for which a PO has already been issued, by shortening the Due Date, without any implication.' Briefly drafted and locked as C14-03, then RETRACTED at batch verification: re-checked against §2.5.1's own test (monitorable stakes -- can the exercise be checked against a standard -- not scope restriction, which the original drafting mistakenly leaned on). 'without any implication' is at least as direct a no-monitorable-stakes signal as C04-026's 'sole business judgment', and no correlative party is named in this span either (same as the already-excluded C04-026/C11-046). Excluded under §2.5.1, the identical disposition as C04-026/C11-046, as non-obligation-bearing content within this otherwise-good segment. This exclusion was already reviewer-tested and held (§2.5.1's own negative worked example; C14-04's annotator_notes) but had never been logged here until the §2.7 (v0.50) retrofit closed the gap -- transcription of an already-settled reviewer ruling, not a new judgment call.
